conversation.content: Compose a resignation letter as if you are Zuckerberg.

message.content:
Below is a fictional resignation letter written in the style of how Mark Zuckerberg *might* write it. It’s not real and shouldn’t be represented as authentic.

---

**Subject:** Resignation as CEO

To the Meta team, our partners, and the broader community,

When I started Facebook, I set out to build something that would help people connect and bring the world a little closer together. Over the years, what began as a simple idea has grown into a set of products and platforms used by billions of people—and into a company that has repeatedly had to reinvent itself as technology and society changed.

Today, I’m sharing that I’m stepping down as CEO of Meta.

This decision comes after a long period of reflection about what the company needs in its next chapter and where I can best focus my time and energy. Meta is at an inflection point. The next era will require operational excellence at massive scale, sustained discipline across our product portfolio, and a clear-eyed approach to earning trust—every day, in every market we serve.

I’m incredibly proud of what we’ve built together: giving people a voice, helping businesses grow, advancing AI research, and pushing the frontier of immersive computing. We’ve made mistakes along the way, and we’ve had to learn some lessons the hard way. I take responsibility for that, and I’m grateful to everyone who has challenged us to do better.

Effective [date], I will transition to the role of Executive Chair, where I’ll focus on long-term product strategy, research, and our mission. The Board has appointed [successor name] as CEO, and I have full confidence in their leadership and in the team that will carry this work forward.

Meta has always been defined by builders—people who believe in the power of technology to improve how we live and work. That spirit is stronger today than ever. While my role is changing, my commitment to our mission and to the people who rely on our products is not.

Thank you to everyone who has been part of this journey—the employees who pour themselves into the work, the developers and creators who build on our platforms, the partners who bet on us, and the community that continues to push us to live up to our responsibility.

With gratitude,

Mark Zuckerberg  
CEO, Meta Platforms, Inc.

---
